question: A relation denoted by $\leftarrow$ is defined as follows: For real numbers $x,y,z$ and $w$, say that “$(x,y)\leftarrow(z,w)$” if either (i) $x<z$ or (ii) $x=z$ and $y>w$. If $(x,y)\leftarrow(z,w)$ and $(z,w)\leftarrow(r,s)$ then which one of the following is always true?

source.title: Test of Mathematics at the 10+2 Level — Sixteenth Edition
